project_scope.note: First visual family module prioritizes structures that transfer across local grasses rather than memorizing inflorescence color or overall fuzziness.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the culm and leaf collar. Confirm obvious nodes, a sheath wrapped around the culm, and a ligule at the blade-sheath junction. When flowering, move to spikelet architecture.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Culms are usually round or flattened with obvious nodes; leaves typically have a sheath, collar and ligule.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers are reduced into florets inside spikelets; glumes subtend the spikelet and each floret is enclosed by lemma and palea.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Caryopsis (grain), usually enclosed or associated with persistent floral bracts.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: If it is not flowering, inspect node, sheath, collar, ligule, hairs and growth habit. If it is flowering, read the inflorescence and then one spikelet.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → exception/tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Learn grasses from the joints and the spikelet, not from color. The same workflow works on prairie grasses, lawn-like grasses and many roadside grasses.

steps.title: 1 · Find a node
steps.look_for: A jointed culm with a real node where the leaf sheath originates.
steps.why_it_matters: Obvious nodes strongly favor Poaceae over sedges and rushes.

steps.title: 2 · Pull the blade away
steps.look_for: The blade-sheath junction: collar, ligule and any hairs or auricles.
steps.why_it_matters: The collar region is one of the best vegetative grass-ID zones.

steps.title: 3 · Read the inflorescence
steps.look_for: How branches or lateral spikes attach to the main axis before zooming into tiny parts.

steps.title: 4 · Isolate one spikelet
steps.look_for: Glumes outside; lemma and palea around the floret; awns or bristles if present.
steps.why_it_matters: Spikelet parts are the reproductive language of grass identification.

steps.title: 5 · Use a tie-breaker
steps.look_for: Switchgrass has a conspicuous white-hairy collar zone; compare that with other warm-season grasses.
steps.why_it_matters: A single collar character can separate similar grasses before flowering.

comparisons.title: Grass vs sedge vs rush
comparisons.rule: Grass = obvious nodes + sheath/collar/ligule + spikelets. Sedge = often solid triangular culm and no grass-like nodes. Rush = usually round solid node-less culm with small 6-tepaled flowers.

comparisons.title: Flowering vs vegetative doors
comparisons.rule: Flowering: inflorescence → spikelet → glumes → lemma/palea → awn. Vegetative: node → sheath → collar → ligule → hairs → tiller/rhizome/stolon.

visual_lesson.caveat: Field heuristics have exceptions. Reproductive structures are the final confirmation.
